main_text.p: regionem ducere non possent, sed ut ne singuli quidem hostem effugerent, qui transire conarentur. Hac Amilcar vi-dens, &c. Idem Polybius libro eodem belli hujus ejusdem causas & initia exponens de Tunete oppido Carthagini vicino sic ait: Mercenarii irâ succensi adversus Carthaginienses, infesti ad urbem feruntur; & quindecim millia passuum ab eâ Tunete castra ponunt. Erant bisupra viginti millia. Tum demum Carthaginiensibus error suus ob oculos obversari, cum nihil eos sera poenitentia juvabat. Et post pauca memorat, Gescon-em ducem ad placandos eosdem hos iratos milites cum pecuniâ ex urbe Carthagine missum, profectumque mari Tunetem appulisse: ubi verba Graeca cum aliis sic habent: O' Γίσκων [illegible, ~10 letters] μ̔ [?] τ̓ χεν-μάτων, [?] [illegible, ~8 letters] τ Τύ-νητα, τὸ μὲν [?] [illegible, ~10 letters] ἡγεμόνας, &c. Quae verba significare videntur, per mare navigari potuisse & appelli Tunetem. Iudicium lectori relinquo. Et rursum idem libro xiv. Tunes Carthagine abest stadia quasi cxx. Locus cum operibus tum suapte naturâ, sicut jam ante ostendimus, tutus, quique ex omni fere parte Carthaginis potest

page.notes: Greek text (Polybius quotation) is only partly legible in the scan: the first word Γίσκων is clear, but most of the following Greek words are illegible or uncertain and are marked accordingly. "Gescon-em" in the text should read "Gesco-nem" as printed: the line-end hyphen is after "Gesco", and the word is rendered as printed with that hyphen. Some words are set in italic type that could not be fully confirmed, and italic extent is approximate. "bisupra" is read from a slightly blurred "bi" plus long-s "supra". The catchword "con-" sits alone at the lower right below the last line of text.
